title: Weak-coupling altermagnetism and chiral magnetic excitations in a checkerboard lattice
authors: Abhigya Rangari, Manna Paul, Sayandip Ghosh
abstract: Altermagnets, characterized by spin-split electronic bands with compensated magnetic moments, have emerged as a new class of magnetic materials garnering attention in recent years. Here, using a minimal one-band Hubbard model, we show that the checkerboard lattice serves as a natural platform for altermagnetism for electrons. The instability towards altermagnetic order is denoted by diverging altermagnetic susceptibility at weak-coupling. Carrying out mean-field treatment of the Hubbard repulsion, we show phase transitions from the nonmagnetic to altermagnetic semimetal and then to altermagnetic insulating phase, allowing clear identification of spin-split states. We then examine magnetic excitations in the altermagnetic phases using a random-phase approximation treatment of the dynamical spin susceptibility. The altermagnetic order is found to be stable against spin-fluctuations with the excitation spectra showing well-defined magnon excitations, which decay into single-particle excitations with decreasing interaction strength. Remarkably, the magnetic excitations exhibit strong dependence on both chirality and direction, showing an alternating chirality splitting, similar to the alternating spin splitting of the electronic bands, which serves as a salient feature of altermagnetism.
summary: This work theoretically explores altermagnetism in a checkerboard lattice using the Hubbard model. By analyzing susceptibility divergences and performing RPA calculations, the authors map out phase transitions to novel magnetic states. The key finding is the observation of chirality-dependent magnon excitations that confirm the unique nature of altermagnetic order.
main_problem: The study investigates weak-coupling altermagnetism and the associated chiral magnetic excitations within a checkerboard lattice structure.
main_result: The research predicts phase transitions from nonmagnetic to altermagnetic semimetal and insulating phases, showing that magnetic excitations exhibit a characteristic alternating chirality splitting mirroring the electronic band splitting.
method: Theoretical calculations employing mean-field treatments of the Hubbard repulsion combined with Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) for analyzing dynamical spin susceptibilities.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a minimal one-band Hubbard model applied to electrons on a checkerboard lattice. The analysis explores how electron interactions drive the material into an altermagnetic state characterized by spin-split bands.
key_observables: Altermagnetic susceptibility ($\chi_{AM}$), spin susceptibility ($\chi_S$), electronic band structure ($E_\pm(\mathbf{k})$), and magnon excitation spectra ($	ext{Im}(\chi)$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($U$) relative to hopping parameters ($t_1, t_2, t_3$); filling level (half-filling).
main_assumptions: The analysis is conducted within a weak-coupling framework and relies on the Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) for excitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lattice structure, static and RPA susceptibilities ($\chi_{AM}$ vs $\mathbf{q}$), phase diagrams showing transitions between different magnetic/electronic phases, spin-resolved band structures, and magnon spectral functions ($	ext{Im}(\chi)$).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the model on the checkerboard lattice, using mean-field theory to map out phase transitions based on $U$, and finally applying RPA techniques to calculate the magnetic excitation spectra in the resulting altermagnetic phases.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the study of spin excitations (magnons) derived from Hubbard models provides insights into collective quantum dynamics that can be relevant for understanding strongly correlated quantum materials studied in AMO physics or condensed matter theory.
